title: What Is the Best Fertilizer Calculator App for Farms in the Philippines?
metaTitle: Fertilizer Calculator App: How to Choose One for Your Farm
metaDescription: Choosing a fertilizer calculator app? Check that it reads local bag grades, counts N, P and K per hectare, uses your soil test and dates every split.
excerpt: The best fertilizer calculator app for a Filipino farm reads the bag grades sold here, adds up nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium per hectare and compares them with what your crop needs. It should also use your soil test and help you time each split. For rice, PhilRice's MOET app and the Rice Crop Manager give recommendations, often with an extension worker's help. anee.io, a farm app built for Filipino farmers, has NPK Plus, a free calculator that also ties the plan to your dated calendar and your stock.

blocks.text:
A fertilizer calculator does two jobs. It turns a recommendation into bags you can buy, and it checks a bag plan you already have against what the crop needs. The math is simple, but it is easy to slip when you juggle three nutrients, five grades and a lot that is not exactly one hectare.

No single app is best for every farm. So start with what the app must do, then see which tools do it for your crop.

items: **Local grades:** it should know 14 14 14, 16 20 0, 46 0 0, 21 0 0 and 0 0 60, and let you add a label of your own.
**Per hectare and per lot:** it should show the nutrients for one hectare and for your real area.
**A crop target:** it should compare your plan with a DA or PhilRice rate and flag what is short or too much.
**Your soil:** it should use a soil test or MOET result when you have one.
**Timing:** the best tools also split the dose by growth stage and put it on a date.

blocks.text: PhilRice says the MOET app gives a recommendation in 60 seconds or less once the pot test is done, and works without an internet connection. The Rice Crop Manager started in 2013 as a free web tool and Android app from IRRI and PhilRice. In 2022 PhilRice reported that DA PhilRice and DA ICT run its advisory service, with land areas checked by GPS.
How does NPK Plus in anee.io compare?

[NPK Plus](/features/npk-plus-calculator) is free on every anee.io plan, Libre included. Tap the fertilizers you plan to use and it adds up every nutrient, as the element and as the oxide, per hectare and for the whole area. It counts micronutrients and biofertilizers too, then marks each nutrient short, right or too much for your crop.

There are honest limits. NPK Plus does not test your soil, so a soil test or MOET result still gives the better base. Its yield line shows what the fertilizer alone can feed, not the harvest you will get. Asking Anee, the smart farm technician, to read the plan against your place, soil and season needs internet and uses credits. The free Libre plan also shows a few ads and keeps one active season.

A calculator answers how much. A season also needs when, and how much is left in the shed. In the [Protocol Builder](/features/protocol-builder), each fertilizer task sits on its day after sowing, transplanting or planting. The protocol then becomes your [cropping calendar](/features/cropping-calendar), and on Solo Farmer the inventory shows what is left to buy.

items.title: Add your fertilizers
items.text: Tap each product you plan to use and type how much, in bags or kilos.

items.title: Read the balance
items.text: Check nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium per hectare against the rate for your crop.

items.title: Fix what is off
items.text: Swap or add a grade until nothing reads short or too much. Our guide to [fertilizer calculation](/blog/fertilizer-calculation) shows the same math by hand.

items.title: Put each dose on a date
items.text: Write the splits into your protocol so every lot gets them on the right day.

blocks.title: Check the plan you were given, and the bags you actually bought
blocks.text: Dealers sometimes swap a grade when stock runs out. Run the calculator again with what you really carried home, so a missing bag of potash shows up before panicle initiation, not after harvest.

items.q: Is there a free fertilizer calculator app in the Philippines?
items.a: Yes. NPK Plus in anee.io is free on every plan, including the free Libre plan. IRRI and PhilRice also launched the Rice Crop Manager in 2013 as a free web tool and Android app for rice.

items.q: Can a fertilizer calculator replace a soil test?
items.a: No. A calculator adds up what you plan to apply, but only a soil test, MOET or a field tool shows what your soil already supplies. Use the test to set the target, then the calculator to hit it.

items.q: Which app works for corn and vegetables, not only rice?
items.a: The MOET app and the Rice Crop Manager are built for rice. NPK Plus in anee.io compares your plan with the usual rate for other crops too, including corn and vegetables.

items.q: Do I need internet to use a fertilizer app?
items.a: PhilRice says the MOET app works without an internet connection. In anee.io, asking Anee to read your fertilizer plan needs internet and uses credits.
